description: Runs the Tracker from the patch: starts and stops it, clocks it from outside and steps through its patterns

params.text: Chooses what the run jack plays: Pattern loops the selected pattern on its own, Song plays the whole timeline
Chooses how the run jack is read: Trigger toggles between playing and stopped on each rising edge, Gate plays while the voltage is at or above 5V and stops below it
Chooses how the clock jack is read: 24, 48 or 96 rising edges to the beat, or Phase, where the voltage itself is the position, 0V at the start of the pattern or the track and 10V at its end
Selects the pattern after the one selected, wrapping round to the first
Selects the pattern before the one selected, wrapping round to the last
Selects one of the track's patterns at random

inputs.text: Starts and stops the track; whether a rising edge toggles it or the voltage has to stay high is set by the switch beside it
Drives the track's clock from outside; what the voltage means is set by CLOCK MODE, and while a cable is here the Tracker's own BPM knob no longer sets the tempo
A rising edge stops the track and puts its clock back to the beginning
A rising edge selects the pattern after the one selected, wrapping round to the first
A rising edge selects the pattern before the one selected, wrapping round to the last
A rising edge selects one of the track's patterns at random

notes: this does nothing until a Tracker module is in the patch, and only the first of these modules takes control of it; a second one is ignored.
the clock jack is read only while the track is playing, so it has to be started from the run jack or from the Tracker's own buttons first.
the three pattern buttons are not in index order: reading the panel left to right they are previous, next and random.
